name: Nuprl
note: proof development system based on constructive computational type theory
typeSystem: Constructive (intuitionistic) computational type theory in the Martin-Lof tradition: types are defined by how their members compute and propositions are types. Proofs are refinement trees whose rule-specific extraction forms compose into a computational witness or program.
runtime: Historically implemented in Lisp, with proofs built interactively as a refinement tree; a verified program is extracted from a completed proof and can then be evaluated.

runtimes.name: Lisp-hosted proof engine (classic Nuprl)
runtimes.role: The original Cornell implementation ran the refinement logic and term evaluator inside a Lisp environment.

runtimes.name: Extracted program evaluator
runtimes.role: Evaluates the program term extracted from a completed constructive proof.

compilers.name: Nuprl refiner
compilers.role: Interactively refines a goal into subgoals until each is proved by a primitive rule, building a proof tree from which a witness term can be extracted.

codeExample.caption: Conceptual refinement outline (schematic pseudocode, not literal Nuprl input)
codeExample.source:
GOAL: for every n in the natural numbers, fact(n) > 0
REFINE by induction on n
  BASE GOAL: fact(0) > 0
  STEP GOAL: from fact(n) > 0, prove fact(n + 1) > 0
